alerts.name: SQL Injection
alerts.desc: SQL injection may be possible. The user-supplied input in the search query parameter is directly concatenated into a dynamic SQLite command without parameterized sanitization. An attacker can manipulate backend queries, extract user password hashes, or bypass authentication.
alerts.solution: Refactor database access to use parameterized prepared statements or an Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) with strict query binding. Never concatenate user-supplied input directly into SQL strings.

alerts.name: Cross Site Scripting (Reflected)
alerts.desc: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was identified in the feedback submission endpoint. Malicious JavaScript injected via the comment parameter is echoed verbatim into the client DOM without HTML entity encoding.
alerts.solution: Contextually encode all user-controlled data before rendering into HTML, JavaScript, CSS, or URL attributes. Implement a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP).

alerts.name: Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens
alerts.desc: No Anti-CSRF tokens were found in the state-changing HTML submission forms. Attackers can forge cross-origin POST requests on behalf of authenticated users.
alerts.solution: Implement cryptographically strong Synchronizer CSRF tokens or configure SameSite=Lax/Strict cookie attributes on session identifiers.

alerts.name: Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
alerts.desc: The HTTP response does not include the X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors header. The application can be framed in malicious third-party websites.
alerts.solution: Configure the web server to emit 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none';'.

alerts.name: Cookie No HttpOnly Flag
alerts.desc: A cookie has been set without the HttpOnly attribute. This permits client-side JavaScript scripts to access the cookie value, increasing risk of credential exfiltration via XSS.
alerts.solution: Ensure that the HttpOnly flag is set on sensitive session and token cookies.

alerts.alert: Server Leaks Information via 'X-Powered-By' HTTP Response Header
alerts.name: Server Leaks Information via 'X-Powered-By' HTTP Response Header
alerts.desc: The web server response reveals internal runtime details via the 'X-Powered-By: Express' header. This assists threat actors in fingerprinting specific software versions.
alerts.solution: Disable or strip the X-Powered-By header in Express middleware: app.disable('x-powered-by').

alerts.name: Remote Code Execution (Template Injection)
alerts.desc: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) allows remote attackers to evaluate arbitrary template expressions within the server runtime, potentially leading to arbitrary system command execution.
alerts.solution: Do not pass untrusted user input directly into template engines. Use logic-less templates or execute templates within strict sandboxes.

alerts.name: Re-examine Cache-Control Directives
alerts.desc: The response contains sensitive customer data but specifies non-restrictive cache controls. Shared proxies or browser caches could store sensitive responses.
alerts.solution: Verify cache control directives for sensitive authenticated endpoints (Cache-Control: no-store).
